About Vanguard Golf Management

Vanguard Golf Management is a premier developer and full-service operator of high-quality golf courses, country clubs, and luxury recreational facilities. Our prestigious portfolio features legendary properties across the Wasatch Front and Mountain West regions, including Thanksgiving Point Golf Club, The Ranches Golf Club, Coral Canyon, and The Ranch Club in Montana.
Beyond manicured fairways, our properties deliver complete resort experiences—comprising fine dining, full-scale event spaces, aquatic complexes, and fitness centers. We bridge traditional personal service with modern digital capability to offer flawless member and public golf experiences.

The Role

We are seeking an executive, hospitality-minded Senior IT Director
to lead our comprehensive enterprise technology strategy, cloud-infrastructure development, and on-site hospitality tech operations. Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer (COO), you will design and implement the technological roadmap that supports both our remote corporate back-office and our brick-and-mortar hospitality facilities.
The ideal candidate will have extensive experience aligning retail POS, real-time booking engines, property management systems (PMS), and distributed IoT/network architectures across multiple geolocations. This role operates in a remote capacity with an expectation to drive modern digital scaling across all owned and operated courses.

What You’ll Do (Responsibilities)

Omnichannel Tech Leadership:
Formulate and execute Vanguard’s enterprise-wide IT strategy, modernizing member portals, e-commerce layers, and frictionless mobile tee-time booking architectures
.
Hospitality Infrastructure & ERP Governance:
Manage the implementation, integration, and daily resilience of property management systems (PMS), club management software (e.g., Clubessential, Jonas), multi-site POS systems, and procurement ERPs.
IoT & Physical Site Connectivity:
Oversee secure connectivity infrastructure for distributed clubs, including guest/member Wi-Fi architectures, club-house IoT systems, smart golf-cart GPS dispatch configurations, and remote agronomy sensor networks.
Cybersecurity & Compliance:
Enforce enterprise information security frameworks (NIST, CIS), ensuring absolute data confidentiality for high-net-worth members and full PCI-DSS compliance across all physical and online payment rails.
Vendor & Lifecycle Management:
Negotiate master service agreements (MSAs) and SLAs with core SaaS providers, custom application development vendors, and hardware logistics providers to optimize IT spend.
Cross-Functional Helpdesk Ops:
Scale a high-performing IT support organization capable of serving asynchronous hospitality operations (covering early-morning turf operations to late-night club events).

Who You Are (Requirements)

Experience:
10+ years of progressive corporate IT leadership experience, with at least 4+ years as an IT Director or Senior Manager overseeing multi-unit hospitality, country club, retail, or property management technology portfolios.
Industry Domain Acumen:
Deep familiarity with tech ecosystems tailored to luxury hospitality, golf course clubhouses, food & beverage (F&B) management, or fractional resort operations.
Technical Breadth:
Practical experience governing cloud networks (AWS/Azure), mobile-first application lifecycles, cross-site Identity & Access Management (IAM), and multi-location hardware provisioning.
Execution & Availability:
Exceptional English communication skills to collaborate seamlessly with property General Managers, PGA Coaches, and corporate executives. Ability to manage a flexible schedule to align with weekend and event-driven operational needs.
Travel Flexibility:
Willingness to travel up to 20% to regional property sites (primarily Utah and Montana) for critical system deployment audits or infrastructure upgrades.
Education:
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Management Information Systems (MIS), Hospitality Management Systems, or a related field. Advanced technical or project management credentials (PMP, ITIL, CISM) are preferred.

jobs.description:
Position Summary

Reporting to the Sr. Director of IT Technology, we are seeking a polished, technical Director of IT Architecture who will be responsible for leading the overall IT architecture strategy for our dynamic, growing healthcare organization. This individual will be tasked with designing systems that align with business goals, regulatory requirements, and emerging industry technologies. This role manages a talented team of IT Network, Cloud, and Systems Architects, overseeing the design, implementation, and optimization of all enterprise technology solutions. The Director works closely with IT leadership and business stakeholders to drive innovation, improve system interoperability, optimize cost and enhance security across the healthcare organization.

Position: Director IT Architecture

Department: Information Technology

Schedule: Full Time

Essential Responsibilities / Duties

Strategic Leadership & Technology Roadmap

Define and execute a comprehensive IT architecture strategy aligned with business, clinical, and operational goals.
Lead and manage a team specializing in network, cloud, and systems architecture, ensuring seamless collaboration and efficiency.
Establish and enforce IT governance, standards, and best practices to ensure compliance with industry regulations (HIPAA, HITECH, HITRUST, etc.).
Evaluate and integrate emerging technologies (microservices, AI, ML) to improve healthcare delivery and operational efficiency.
Provide strategic direction for IT infrastructure, ensuring high availability, scalability, and performance optimization.
Strong financial acumen, ensuring positive ROI for Architecture-led initiatives.

Architectural Leadership & Implementation

Responsible for all aspects of the Network Architecture, ensuring secure, reliable, and high-performance network infrastructure to support healthcare applications and data exchange.
Responsible for all aspects of the Cloud Architecture initiatives, including hybrid and multi-cloud strategies, ensuring compliance, cost optimization, and interoperability with on-premises systems.
Guide Systems Architecture development, ensuring robust design, security, and integration of core business and healthcare applications, including EHR/EMR (Epic).

Collaboration & Stakeholder
Engagement

Act as the primary liaison between IT architecture teams and IT leadership, translating business needs into technology strategies.
Partner with IT Security team to develop and enforce security frameworks that protect patient data and mitigate cybersecurity threats.
Partner with Cloud team to establish common tooling and automation (e.g., CloudFormation, AWS CDK, AWS Landing Zone Accelerator, Terraform, Kubernetes, Docker, Jenkins).
Work closely with software vendors, system integrators, and cloud service providers to optimize technology investments.
Foster collaboration across cross-functional IT teams, ensuring alignment with infrastructure, security, and application teams.

Performance Management & Risk Mitigation

Establish KPIs and performance metrics to evaluate the effectiveness of IT architecture initiatives.
Identify and mitigate risks related to network vulnerabilities, cloud security, and system failures.
Optimize IT spending by implementing cost-effective solutions.
Continuously assess system performance and scalability to meet the growing demands of healthcare operations.

(The above statements in this job description are intended to depict the general nature and level of work assigned to the employee(s) in this job. The above is not intended to represent an exhaustive list of accountable duties and responsibilities required).

REQUIRED EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:

Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Information Technology, Healthcare Informatics, or a related field.
10+ years of progressive experience in IT architecture, including at least 5 years in a leadership role managing network, cloud, and systems architecture teams preferably within a healthcare organization.
Network Architecture: Strong experience with SD-WAN, VPNs, firewalls, network security protocols, and healthcare data exchange networks.
Cloud Architecture: Strong experience with AWS, Well-Architected Framework, and hybrid cloud solutioning.
Demonstrated history of assessing, testing, implementing modern platform visibility solutions (DataDog, Dynatrace, New Relic, Prometheus / Grafana).

Preferred Education And Experience

Recent certifications in relevant cloud platforms (AWS Certified: Solutions Architect Professional, AWS Security Specialty, etc Microsoft Certified: Azure Solutions Architect, etc.)
CISSP, CCNP, HITRUST, or FinOps Certification

Systems Architecture: Expertise in the M365 suite, server infrastructure, virtualization, storage solutions, disaster recovery, and healthcare IT standards (HL7, FHIR, DICOM, etc.).
Security & Compliance: Knowledge of HIPAA & HITRUST compliance, and cybersecurity frameworks (NIST CSF, ISO27K). Ability to work cross-functionally with the BMCHS Information Security Team to define and design according to industry best-practice.
Fluency in Agile, waterfall, and industry standard tooling (e.g., Jira, Project, Confluence).
Strong leadership and team management skills. You are a thought-leader and a mentor.
Excellent communication and stakeholder management abilities. You have excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills.

Our team of senior professionals delivers a wide array of strategic advisory, shareholder advisory, restructuring and special situations and private fund advisory and placement services to corporations, financial sponsors, institutional investors and governments around the world. We offer a unique portfolio of advisory services designed to help our clients achieve their strategic objectives. From the beginning, PJT Partners has firmly believed that having the best people is key to building an enduring franchise. Our perspective was, and remains, that a great team brings in both top tier clients and appeals to a wide-range of diverse, talented colleagues. Fostering an inclusive culture, which welcomes differing perspectives and beliefs, enables us to provide the best advice and insights to our clients.

To learn more about PJT Partners, please visit our website at www.pjtpartners.com.

Responsibilities

The Technology department at PJT is responsible for creating and continuously improving a robust and secure technology foundation that supports the firm's business activities. As artificial intelligence becomes deeply embedded in both internal operations and the broader vendor ecosystem, the firm faces a new and rapidly evolving risk surface. The AI Security & Risk Manager will be PJT's dedicated subject matter expert at the intersection of AI and security, helping the firm navigate this landscape with rigor and clarity.

We are seeking a high-performing AI Security & Risk professional to join the Cybersecurity team. Reporting to the Head of Technology Risk, this individual will own the firm's approach to identifying, assessing, and managing risk introduced by AI — both through internal AI deployments and through vendors increasingly embedding AI into their platforms. The role requires a practitioner who can operate at both a strategic and technical level: fluent in AI architecture and threat modeling while equally capable of communicating risk clearly to senior leadership and regulators. The candidate must build strong relationships across Technology, Legal, Compliance, and the business to ensure AI risk is managed as an enterprise priority, not a silo.

Additional Responsibilities Include

AI Risk Governance & Strategy

Own and maintain the firm's AI risk framework, covering model risk, data privacy, adversarial threats, third-party AI, and regulatory compliance.
Develop and enforce AI usage policies in collaboration with Legal and Compliance, including acceptable use, data classification requirements, and prompt handling standards.
Maintain an inventory of AI tools deployed firm-wide — both sanctioned and shadow — and assess associated risk profiles.
Provide regular AI risk reporting to the Head of Technology Risk and senior leadership, including emerging threat trends, vendor posture changes, and control gaps.
Monitor the evolving regulatory environment for AI (EU AI Act, SEC guidance, DORA, NY DFS) and advise on compliance obligations and required controls.

Vendor AI Evaluation & Third-Party Risk

Lead security and risk assessments of vendors introducing AI capabilities into existing or new platforms, including evaluating model transparency, data handling practices, and auditability.
Develop and maintain a structured AI vendor evaluation framework, incorporating criteria for model governance, output reliability, data residency, and incident response obligations.
Partner with Procurement and Legal to ensure AI-specific provisions are reflected in vendor contracts, including data usage restrictions, model change notifications, and liability terms.
Maintain a tiered risk register of third-party AI integrations, with ongoing monitoring for material changes to vendor AI functionality, architecture, or ownership.
Engage directly with vendor security and product teams to assess AI-related controls and drive remediation of identified gaps.

AI Threat Modeling & Security Architecture

Conduct threat modeling for AI systems and integrations, including risks from prompt injection, model inversion, training data poisoning, and adversarial inputs.
Evaluate AI-specific attack surfaces introduced by LLM integrations, agentic workflows, and MCP-connected data sources.
Collaborate with infrastructure and application teams to embed AI security controls into deployment pipelines and system design reviews.
Assess risks associated with AI-generated content, including deepfake vectors, synthetic phishing, and automated social engineering in the context of financial services.
Contribute to the firm's broader security architecture by ensuring AI components are assessed within the existing control framework.

Internal AI Program Oversight

Serve as the security and risk point of contact for the firm's internal AI deployments, including Claude Enterprise and any future platform integrations.
Evaluate data retention, access control, and logging practices for AI platforms to ensure alignment with the firm's compliance and eDiscovery obligations.
Provide risk assessments for proposed AI use cases across the firm, including a structured framework for approving, conditionally approving, or declining adoption.
Support audit and compliance reviews related to AI, including evidence collection and engagement with regulators or external assessors as required.
Develop and deliver AI security awareness content for technology staff and end users.

Qualifications

PJT Partners seeks to hire individuals who are highly motivated, intelligent and have demonstrated excellence in prior endeavors. In addition, qualified candidates will possess the following:

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Security, Data Science, or a related field; advanced degree a plus.
At least 7–10 years of experience in information security, technology risk, or a related field, with a minimum of 3 years focused on AI systems, machine learning security, or AI governance.
Deep understanding of the AI and LLM landscape, including foundation model architecture, agentic systems, RAG pipelines, and the risk implications of each.
Hands-on experience evaluating AI platforms and products, including the ability to assess vendor claims about model behavior, data handling, and security controls with appropriate skepticism.
Familiarity with AI risk frameworks and emerging standards, including NIST AI RMF, MITRE ATLAS, OWASP LLM Top 10, and ISO/IEC 42001.
Experience with vendor risk management in a regulated financial services environment, including contract negotiation support and third-party security assessments.
Knowledge of relevant regulatory frameworks including DORA, SOX, SEC cybersecurity disclosure rules, and GDPR/CCPA as they apply to AI data flows.
Strong technical skills sufficient to evaluate AI system architecture, API security, data pipeline design, and access control models without reliance solely on vendor documentation.
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to translate highly technical AI risk concepts into clear, decision-ready language for senior leadership, Legal, and Compliance.
Experience operating in a Microsoft-first environment, including familiarity with Entra ID, Azure, and M365 security tooling, is a strong plus.
Ability to work independently, manage competing priorities, and operate effectively in a fast-paced, lean team environment
Relevant certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CRISC, or emerging AI-focused credentials a plus

Reporting to the Head of Technology Risk, this individual will own the firm's approach to identifying, assessing, and managing risk introduced by AI — both through internal AI deployments and through vendors increasingly embedding AI into their platforms. Define what a modern IT function looks like at Engine — device lifecycle, endpoint security, internal tooling, integrations. Retire what shouldn't exist. Consolidate what should.
Own identity and automation:
Architect Okta as Engine's single source of truth for identity, access, and automation. Onboarding, offboarding, provisioning, access reviews — if it's manual today, it won't be six months from now.

Partner with Security on Okta, SSO, MFA, and access reviews. Ensure that scale never comes at the cost of the basics.

Leadership.

Tech stack fluency.

Player-coach depth.

Security fluency.
You understand the intersection of productivity and protection. You've partnered with security teams on audits, access reviews, endpoint health, and incident response.
AI-curious.

High standards, high judgment.
